docs__orientation.description: Lean current-state orientation. Use a focused feature or subsystem group before reading broader source.
notes: TODO owns executable work and completion conditions.
APP_STATE owns shipped behavior; review.md is opened only for integrity-pass evidence.
The 74 KiB orientation cap accommodates the measured current-state and task-record content; defaults remain two docs under the unchanged 256 KiB generation ceiling.
README launch/format entry remains in issue__verification_current_head and is read directly during task intake; orientation retains current state and the work queue.

workflow__context_bank.description: Portable public context routing, validation, and generation entry points.
notes: Exact files and explicit globs are the only path contract; bare directories fail.
Node.js 22 or newer is the canonical runtime.
Generation never truncates a file or writes when --out - is requested; scans, globs, explicit paths, and trees honor runtime and configured directory exclusions.
Explicit paths reject symlink ancestors and Windows drive-relative escapes.
Public generation uses node scripts/generate-context.mjs --group <group> --out -; private local helper/agent folders are excluded from routes and scans.
Generated text regions normalize CRLF to LF before rendering and budget accounting; source files and binary evidence are never rewritten.

workflow__project_integrity.description: Project-doc and release integrity contracts: TODO and Pitfall Ledger shape, exact Guard targets, palette scope, synchronized app versions, imports, and Rust module declarations.
notes: The guard is local and read-only: it reports missing durable docs, malformed or silently empty backlogs, machine-local paths in current-facing docs, unreviewed inbox notes, unresolved relative frontend imports, and unresolved Rust mod declarations before the application verification lane runs.
The same gate requires stable Pitfall Ledger IDs and existing exact Guard files, Modern-only palette ownership with scoped flat Original rules, and frontend/Cargo/Tauri version equality.
Three.js selection, rig-state, and diagnostic colors are semantic render colors, not decorative UI palette values.
The workspace verify script must retain the same game-ready dependency guard used by run.ps1; the project-integrity regression catches drift between the public npm and launcher entry points.
Palette input contracts are theme-owned in feature__theme_system; stable ledger records are routed in workflow__pitfall_guard_validation.
Relative-import candidates must be files; a bare directory without an index module fails even when the directory itself exists.
Active TODO fields must contain completion criteria and cannot coexist with the empty-backlog marker.
The 0.2.1 preview gate validates first-party MIT metadata, matching lock versions and exact installed notice/sample resource mappings. The measured owner/tests expansion uses a 104 KiB focused cap.

workflow__pitfall_guard_validation.description: Stable Pitfall Ledger records and exact Guard references used to prevent recurring regressions.
notes: The ledger owns numbered PL-001 through PL-062 entries, each with an exact Guard path and Manual evidence only for non-automatable checks.
Use workflow__project_integrity for the implementation and regression test that validates ledger IDs and referenced Guard files.

workflow__git_main_sync.description: Public-source exclusions and the optional private maintainer main-publication contract.
notes: Private .tools/ and .agents/ plus legacy inventory generators are absent from public source and ignored locally. Public context routes cannot require them.

The Node regression runs in run.ps1 verify. With private helpers installed it retains all main-only, configured-origin, non-destructive synchronization and staged-publication checks. With all helpers absent those private checks are explicitly skipped; partial installations fail.

Optional maintainer staged publication binds a file allowlist and expected base/tree to one commit, preserves owner work, rejects remote advancement, and retries a failed push without another commit. Disposable local repositories cover partial staging and failure paths without production credentials.
Public setup and application checks use the launcher routed by tests__quality and do not require private helper or agent installation.

feature__theme_system.description: Persisted themes, Modern model viewer with task drawers, Original presentation, responsive behavior and visual evidence.
notes: Original preserves the old editor's simplicity and compact hierarchy, including quad view before model load.
Modern palette ownership lives in modern.css under the Lumen Alloy theme scope; shared index.css owns layout and behavior, and Original selectors stay explicitly scoped.
The loaded-SMF strict snapshot is owned by tests__browser_shell_lifecycle in shell-model.spec.ts; this group owns the responsive and Original strict captures in visual.spec.ts.
Theme definitions own shell variants, labels, panel copy, camera scale, and grid behavior; shared behavior should not branch on theme IDs.

Modern uses one icon strip and workspace chooser. Tools opens a closed-by-default task drawer; inactive tasks stay mounted. Skin keeps four viewport icons, with its brush card hidden while Tools is open. The full timeline mounts only in Animate.
ViewportControls exposes separate Rig fade and reversible Hide rig/Show rig controls so helper geometry can be removed for shaded-skin inspection without mutating source or export state.
docs/references/theme-qa/README.md owns the preserved-source comparison and final fidelity evidence paths.
The theme cap includes the shared task-shell source and six-size authoring proof; detailed Skin behavior stays in its authoring route.
Shared task navigation and authoring actions are routed in feature__workspace_tasks; Help and concise status behavior retain their preview workflow owner.

feature__model_outliner_materials.description: Model-derived submodel rows, source texture thumbnails, material fallback, and preview/source isolation.
notes: Outliner summaries read registered source materials so viewport previews cannot hide source maps.
Raw SMF DataTexture pixels are downsampled into bounded previews; unsupported images fall back to material color.

feature__game_ready_material_repair.description: Strict OBJ/MTL reference matching, failure-safe material preparation, and portable GLB texture embedding.
notes: UI material repair is a reversible editor transaction; preparation failure disposes every material and texture acquired before the error.

JPEG/PNG inputs are embedded as PNG; signatures and decoded dimensions are validated before repair. Metallic and roughness occupy glTF B/G channels, and source-row flipping is explicit so OBJ and glTF texture coordinates agree.
Generated assets, screenshots, job-specific reports, and private source paths remain under excluded output/runtime locations and must not enter context routes.

feature__rig_retargeting.description: Explicit humanoid rig mapping, sampled clip transfer, and normalized rig-proportion diagnostics. Natural-motion solving has its own focused route.
notes: Opaque numeric rigs require an explicit reviewed map and never fuzzy-match; normalized segment ratios expose proportion mismatches that correct axes alone cannot solve.

Retargeting samples helper-ancestor world motion, transfers mapped swings relative to reference poses, can scope absolute source directions to action limbs, can preserve target terminal or explicitly listed rotations, and supports a bounded trusted-peak recovery envelope for damaged source clips.

Natural motion distributes torso rotation by target segment length, solves target-length two-bone legs, locks calibrated sole contacts with declared root travel, and applies clip-scoped target-pelvis leg-angle and swing-bend limits that fade out at full contact.

Requested-rate resampling evaluates source tracks at float32 frame times so upward-rounded STEP keys are not read one frame early, keeps partial terminal samples inside clip duration, and treats output next-down timing as a separate frame-indexed-consumer contract.
Per-clip local scale transfer is opt-in, neutral-relative, axis-mapped, bounded, and validated against source/target bones; unselected scale tracks remain discarded.

subsystem__natural_motion.description: Target-length torso/leg/contact solving, bounded swing validation, root-travel compensation and regressions; use rig-retargeting for orchestration.

subsystem__endpoint_envelopes.description: Offline target-clip endpoint and pre-contact anchor sampling, fixed-length local pose envelopes, complete STEP TRS emission and post-contact endpoint rejection.

feature__retarget_profiles.description: Portable path-free retarget settings, strict profile editing, and undoable in-app application through the shared retarget core.
notes: The collapsed Animate surface accepts a complete v2 game-ready job or rustsmf.retarget-profile.v1 JSON, reports strict validation errors, and keeps the draft in app-owned state across panel unmounts.
Standalone profiles reject sourceModel and complete-job imports strip it; users select source files at apply time, so saved profiles do not reopen owner-local paths.

React and CLI callers share profileClipOptions for clip naming, reference resolution, preservation, direction, natural-motion, timing, recovery, and scale-transfer settings; application is one animation-history transaction.

workflow__game_ready_cli.description: Versioned local job parsing, bounded input, validation, immutable generation publication, and machine-readable evidence.
notes: The CLI rejects duplicate or input-overwriting paths, ambiguous empty clip selections, unknown attachment roles, non-regular files, per-file overflow, and aggregate overflow before later files are materialized.

Inputs are read sequentially through one open handle per file under the remaining aggregate budget; one global direction-transfer mode replaces repetitive clip declarations while explicit per-clip overrides remain supported.

V2 retains strict OBJ/MTL material repair. V3 preserve-existing accepts self-contained GLB or explicitly selected FBX sidecars, fails closed on missing/unready resources or dropped material assignments, and observes cancellation before the atomic generation commit.
The CLI's Node Three.js image runtime decodes PNG/JPEG pixels and supplies canvas/image behavior for texture readiness and GLB export; it is part of producer identity.

Node Three export honors requested PNG/JPEG MIME with matching signatures; shared header preflight bounds image edges, pixels, JPEG decoder memory, and aggregate decoded RGBA allocations before decode/canvas allocation.

Embedded GLB validation checks image signatures, payload decoding, image buffer references, material texture indices, and one aggregate decoded-image budget; preserve-existing roundtrips asymmetric PNG/JPEG textures across duplicate-named material slots.

Canonical producer and sorted role-tagged input identity select an immutable generation; producer identity hashes the executable local dependency list and package manifests so helper changes cannot retain an older source identity.
Model, normalized job, resolved mapping, and report are staged and fsynced before a last-written hash manifest and one directory rename, then the optional current pointer is replaced.

A neutral two-motion caller-owned job runs through the actual CLI, checks sampled motion/raw skin/decoded material content after re-import, and preserves the prior generation and caller inputs on malformed mapping, missing clip, or injected publication failure; a clean copied tool workspace proves no consumer checkout is required and the production guard rejects game/engine references.
Per-clip scale transfer is opt-in, validated against loaded source/target bones during retargeting, and cannot combine with that clip's pose recovery.
Generated assets, reports, private job paths, and source models stay outside context routes.

workflow__game_ready_neutral_proof.description: Neutral caller-owned saved-job proof, re-import checks, publication rollback, and production dependency boundaries.
notes: The fixture is a small noncombat two-motion rig with caller-supplied mapping and constraints; it invokes the actual saved-job CLI, reimports the published GLB, and checks transforms, timing, skin, material, and provenance.

V3 preserve-existing coverage uses caller-owned textured skinned GLB fixtures, including asymmetric PNG/JPEG images in duplicate-named material slots, and the independent skinned animated FBX. It checks pixel orientation and texture-slot assignments after export/re-import, explicit sidecar resolution, animation/skin round-trip, and cancellation before publication; v2 repair coverage remains separate.

Malformed mapping, missing source clip, and injected publication failure preserve the prior valid generation and caller-owned inputs. The dependency guard rejects fight-game-study/GaimEngine checkout references without making game acceptance a RustSMF concern.
The runtime receipt is generated under excluded test-results output and is evidence only; it is not a context-bank route or source input.

feature__model_outliner_authoring.description: Guarded non-SMF Outliner metadata, static structural/surface authoring, and bounded global history.
notes: Name, visibility, selection, and scoped parent order use one ID-only snapshot owner; history never stores cyclic Three.js scene graphs.
Rename is limited to binding-safe, unique, unanimated GLB/FBX/OBJ objects; SMF source names remain source-owned.
SMF rename, reorder, duplicate, delete, append, and surface-edit controls stay disabled with source-owned guidance; GLB, FBX, and OBJ remain the supported editable source formats.
Reorder swaps only eligible siblings under one parent, preserves non-Outliner children, and is covered by exact undo/redo plus GLB re-import.

Duplicate/delete use explicit parent/index structural operations, independently clone static disposable resources, and reject bones, skinned subtrees, unsupported sources, and animation targets before mutation.

Static append, transforms, named material assignment, winding reversal, and geometry preparation use guarded non-SMF/static targets and the same undoable Outliner snapshot contract; async append commits only when the initiating model root is still current.

feature__fbx_support.description: FBX import with bounded selected texture sidecars, binary FBX 7500 export, pre-save validation, and round-trip coverage.
notes: The bundled exporter is the implementation authority.
Exported bytes must re-import and preserve representative mesh, skin, bone, and clip structure before save.
The independent Blender-authored fixture is test-only; Blender 5.0.0 validates both the source asset and app-exported output, but this does not claim universal FBX compatibility.

FBX texture parsing waits on its isolated loader manager; shared image-readiness implementation and tests live in issue__external_model_resources. Authorized selected relative maps resolve through the shared resource bundle, and unavailable maps fail safe before render.
Game-ready preserve-existing opts into strict resource resolution even for a one-file bundle; ordinary UI import behavior for unresolved absolute or embedded resources is unchanged.

feature__dae_support.description: Collada DAE import/export with visual-scene, static/skinned geometry, joint weights, matrix animation, and bounded round-trip validation.
notes: ColladaLoader is the browser import authority; DAE imports synthesize missing vertex normals and await sidecar image readiness before releasing temporary URLs, while the local serializer writes 1.4.1 Y_UP visual scenes, materials, geometry, controllers, inverse bind matrices, and matrix animation channels.

Export validates by re-importing before save and rejects duplicate joint names or non-triangle geometry. External texture images are not embedded by the DAE writer; use GLB for texture-fidelity export.

Imports keep selected sidecar image URLs alive until bounded readiness settles, then remove and report unavailable maps; user-facing import guidance lives in docs/user/README.md. ZIP archives remain containers, not model inputs; users must extract and select the DAE plus authorized sidecars.
The shared test policy and cross-feature evidence matrix are owned by tests__quality; this route keeps the DAE implementation, direct tests and format guidance.

The 2026-09-20 supplied pair matched on Y_UP/0.01m units, 28 animation channels and 76 timing samples; the with-skin source passed RustSMF start/mid/end single and quad visual inspection with no observed leg/torso failure or self-clipping. This is source-inspection evidence, not game or retarget acceptance.

subsystem__model_geometry_preparation.description: Shared GLB, FBX, DAE, and OBJ geometry-attribute preparation plus loader-safe tangent prerequisites.
notes: Missing preview UVs and normals may be synthesized, but generated zero UVs are not evidence for tangent-space derivation.
Tangent generation requires compatible source UV and normal attributes plus a finite, in-range indexed triangle layout; non-indexed SMF/GLB triangle soup must remain warning-free.

subsystem__smf_codec_worker.description: SMF worker protocol, structural validation, ownership transfer, cancellation, timeout, and startup fallback.
notes: Worker messages are untrusted values.
Canonical editor buffers are cloned before export transfer.
Abort is rechecked after handler setup and before postMessage; runtime worker errors do not silently fall back to the main thread.

subsystem__export_pipeline.description: Current-root conversion, SMF diagnostics, source-state preservation, and serialized save orchestration.
notes: One pure candidate builder must own pose, animation, and live-skin application.
Indexed runtime geometry is expanded to SMF triangle soup before worker validation.
All saves stay globally single-flight and freshness-checked.

issue__glb_roundtrip_identity.description: Stable GLB scene envelopes, authored-root preservation, matrix-only animation guards and repeated roundtrip proof.
notes: Loader-owned identity scene envelopes are exported as scenes, not additional nodes; existing named wrappers are never flattened by guessing.
Authored root transforms and animation require real nodes. Animated export rejects matrix-only transforms that TRS serialization cannot retain.

subsystem__viewport_editor.description: Three.js viewport lifecycle, selection, transform controls, edit gestures, overlays, and layouts.
notes: Mount-owned listeners and controls require one explicit dispose owner.
Long-lived callbacks read current mutable state through refs.
Perspective and orthographic panes keep distinct directions and zoom while sharing one pan/focus target.
Model framing, clip planes, orbit limits, wheel zoom, and orthographic extents scale from finite geometry bounds without mutating the authored model transform.
Animation actions bind only when the mixer root matches the current root; attachment applies one complete current playback intent.
Pending RAF handles are canceled through the shared zero-safe animation-frame guard.

subsystem__viewport_support.description: Viewport-facing bone picking, fail-closed humanoid aliases, labels, highlights, helper geometry, Inspector controls, display lighting, and shared Three guards.
notes: ThreeViewport owns lifecycle and event timing; these directly imported helpers own the leaf rendering, picking, label, and type-guard contracts consumed by it and by loader/rig paths. Rig-helper geometry derives scale from world-space bone spacing and model bounds rather than a fixed world-unit floor.

feature__rig_ik_pose.description: Bone hierarchy, pose editing, rig transforms, persisted rig metadata, endpoint editing, bounded CCD IK, and explicit keyed bake.
notes: Static non-SMF meshes can be promoted to one root-bound skeleton; preparation is reversible through the shared rig history and participates in dirty replacement protection.

Rig metadata persists primary axis, lock, and pin fields through standalone bounded JSON and project envelopes. IK skips locked/pinned joints; explicit solve-and-bake creates one animation history transaction and honors clip locks.
Rig continuity owns structural metadata regression here; the combined IK/key/project story is routed by workflow__frontend_authoring_journeys.

feature__model_diagnostics.description: Read-only geometry, UV, material, shader-capability, handedness, and viewport pose-overlay diagnostics.
notes: Reports are finite and named per-mesh values with explicit shader support notes; they do not mutate source geometry or export bytes.
Rest ghost, current-to-rest trails, and onion-skin lines are viewport-owned disposable helpers and are rebuilt only from current display state.
Retired same-texture merging is diagnostic-only: shared references are reported, but no UV or material-ownership mutation is performed.

feature__animation_authoring.description: Timeline interaction, workspace-aware playback, pose-based clip creation, Bone/Branch/Full Rig key authoring, clip management, metadata, history, and browser ownership.
notes: useLoadModel remains the load/export integration owner; animation authoring actions are delegated to the tested controller contract.

New clips capture the load-time rest pose or current local bone pose, emit position/quaternion keys for named skeleton bones, and use one animation-workspace history transaction even when the source clip list is empty.
Quadratic interpolation is preserved as SMF metadata and previews linearly in Three.js.

Scoped key operations resolve a selected hierarchy, commit one history transaction, union timeline markers, and validate the clipboard's source scope, skeleton fingerprint, and target bone names before mutation.

Animation edit and clipboard maps use null-prototype records so hostile but valid names such as __proto__ cannot become prototype reads or writes; bounded duration set/extension, retime, trim, and locked-bone policy are implemented with one workspace transaction per action.
The viewport advances the mixer imperatively; parent timeline publication is throttled to a 50 ms display cadence while scrub and playback-intent setters remain immediate.

Rig and default Rest / Bind Skin restore the authored rest pose. Explicit Frozen Current Skin evaluates the selected clip/time and pauses it; Live Animation follows playback through the same workspace policy.

feature__skin_authoring.description: Skin paint and regional smoothing, Modern direct-paint chrome, brush indexing, auto-weight algorithms, history, exportability, and browser ownership.
notes: Brush queries use bounded spatial candidates and verify world-space distance before mutation; one mesh index is reused across each stroke instead of traversing the scene per vertex.
Completed strokes and batch actions own one undoable snapshot transaction.

Set paint separates target weight from brush flow and falloff; selected-weight Skin pts refresh posed positions through a non-serializable runtime WeakMap link and provide exact source-vertex paint targets while surface brushing remains the broad-stroke fallback.
Skin diagnostics reads raw four-slot attributes for the hovered vertex and aggregate mesh counts, preserving invalid references/weights as stable issue codes instead of silently clamping them.

Brush sampling exposes Rest / Bind, Frozen Current, and Live Animation modes; workspacePlayback is intentionally shared with animation authoring so the selected sample matches the displayed pose. Frozen Current owns a captured bone-matrix snapshot and Live Animation displays a safety warning.
Weight preview is a non-destructive vertex-color display; original color attributes and material vertex-color modes are restored on disable/export.

Modern starts Skin with a slim Pick/Paint/Erase/Smooth rail and contextual brush card. Tools exposes Brush/Weights/Display; Scene retains shared unsaved/export-block state without brush sliders. Pick selects bones and Smooth needs no selected bone. Original retains its full panel. Workspace task tests own drawer reachability; component tests own clean/dirty/blocked notice rendering.
Batch history comparisons use a mesh/vertex snapshot index rather than repeated linear scans.
Skin undo/redo entries are bounded to 50 entries and 32 MiB per direction; oldest-entry eviction reports through the status surface.

subsystem__smf_format_and_fidelity.description: SMF parsing, serialization, coordinate conversion, rig fidelity, and malformed-input diagnostics.
notes: The TypeScript worker codec is the sole structural SMF authority; the native bridge transports only authorized bounded bytes.
SMF limits are centralized in smfBinary.ts, including the 512 MiB decoded-memory estimate, and must be changed with focused malformed-input tests and APP_STATE documentation.
Tangent handedness is normalized at import and byte-packed at export so the fourth tangent component is not silently discarded.
Envelope validation requires section starts after the header, minimum count widths, strict non-overlap, and an in-file animation count byte.

subsystem__tauri_bridge.description: Tauri command adapters, native file dialogs, authorized bounded reads, staged serialized writes, recovery ownership, and native smoke coverage.
notes: Rust owns native open/save dialogs; reads require a canonical path previously selected by the native dialog, saves do not accept a frontend path, and all blocking file work is capped at 256 MiB.
Native reads open the authorized canonical file once, reject non-regular paths, and reject a stream that grows beyond the same 256 MiB cap after metadata inspection.
The frontend passes a Uint8Array byte view to save_file_binary rather than constructing an explicit Array.from number array; typed IPC remains bounded by the same native limit.

Native Open requires exactly one supported model before reading or replacing authoring state. Native read responses are untrusted: binaryPayload.ts requires one payload per selected file and accepts only ArrayBuffer, Uint8Array, or arrays of integer bytes from 0 through 255 so coercion cannot wrap malformed values.
Rust owns dialog invocation through its pinned tauri-plugin-dialog dependency; the frontend has no unused dialog-plugin package.

The native CSP permits local blob fetches and the WebView2 IPC hostname. Foreground saves await active autosave before opening their destination dialog. All native writes share one async serialization owner, stage and sync complete payloads before replacement, and restore the previous destination when installation fails.
Project recovery discovery and reads accept only the owned target plus .bak1 and .bak2 regular files; arbitrary app-data siblings fail before filesystem access.
The lazy native-client loader shares one in-flight adapter construction and clears rejected imports for retry; direct unit tests cover overlap identity and recovery after failure.

tests__quality.description: Verification contract, test inventory, shared browser fixtures, lint/type gates, and production-boundary checks.

tests__browser_shell_lifecycle.description: Browser shell, model load, async ownership, and worker responsiveness flows.
notes: The Playwright config owns one build-and-preview server for the full suite.
Test titles remain stable after the domain split.
The unit runner discovers every src/**/*.test.ts file in deterministic order; adding a file requires no package-script edit.
Managed Windows Chromium launch can use the process-local RUSTSMF_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE override; the path must be absolute and existing.
Non-SMF-to-SMF browser cases assert the enabled action for compatible skinned sources and diagnostic blocking for static or unsupported sources; source-SMF export cases remain enabled.
Dirty replacement coverage asserts Cancel preserves the mounted model and Discard clears authoring state before the selected model is committed.

The stress fixture supplies triangle metadata for every generated triangle-soup vertex, and overlap tests explicitly confirm each queued replacement so semantic and async regressions fail at the intended boundary.
Native mock coverage is routed through subsystem__tauri_bridge rather than duplicated in this browser shell group.

workflow__recorded_browser_journey.description: Recorded real-SMF hand-wave journey, precision Skin repair, keyed motion and semantic project continuity; shared single-worker journey command.
notes: The targeted hand-wave command retains one recorded 1440x900 DPR 1.25 journey; test:journey runs all eleven stories sequentially with one worker.

workflow__product_continuity_journeys owns core format/project/replacement stories; workflow__frontend_authoring_journeys owns five additional editing stories. tests__quality owns the feature evidence matrix.
All generated video, screenshots, traces and decoded exports remain ignored runtime evidence.

feature__project_recovery.description: Versioned RustSMF project envelopes, bounded browser/native save adapters, rotating recovery generations, and fail-closed restore flows.
notes: The project envelope embeds a validated GLB snapshot and bounded workspace state, including rig metadata, without replacing asset export formats.
Project state validation reuses the supported model-format registry, so every supported source format, including DAE, survives project round-trip while the embedded asset remains GLB.

Native writes are serialized and use unique staged files; project save rotates bounded generations with restoration on failure, while recovery discovery/read accepts only the exact owned regular-file generations.

Foreground saves remain single-flight. Autosave coalesces work to the newest trailing request while a write is active; successful model replacement invalidates queued old-model work and waits for an issued write before swapping roots, while canceled/failed pickers leave recovery work intact.

A refused recovery write surfaces a Save Project action without losing prior recovery bytes or live edits. A current successful retry clears only the autosave-owned error; unrelated errors remain visible. The browser quota regression proves manual project bytes and resumed recovery through ordinary edits.
Focused project-recovery.spec.ts proves serialized state and continued save; native.spec.ts write/race coverage remains in subsystem__tauri_bridge.

issue__smf_conversion_spatial_fidelity.description: Validated non-SMF-to-SMF conversion boundary, coordinate ownership, rig parent resolution, and numeric parity routes.
notes: The app enables non-SMF-to-SMF save and SMF roundtrip actions for compatible skinned single-root sources, including prepared static FBX/OBJ roots; unprepared static roots, scale tracks, malformed geometry, and semantic failures remain blocked.
The builder keeps mesh arrays in model-root Three space, captures root-relative world DQs, and samples clips through a cloned Three mixer; the serializer owns the single Three-to-SMF vector boundary.
Numeric tests cover non-identity mesh transforms, nested rig matrices, and mixer quaternion interpolation before browser-facing use.

issue__verification_current_head.description: Current working-tree verification evidence, authoritative local gates, browser result classification, and cleanup ownership.
notes: review.md owns the latest assessment; HISTORY.md owns dated command evidence and TODO.md owns forward work. APP_STATE.md supplies broader product contracts only when needed.
Use the test:e2e:list package script for browser inventory so npm cannot consume Playwright's --list flag and accidentally run the suite.

Classify browser failures by assertion, launch, and teardown phase; a historical managed-process caveat must never hide a current product assertion failure, and runner-owned ports must be clear after interrupted runs.
tests__quality owns the full feature evidence matrix; this route keeps command and current-review ownership.

issue__external_model_resources.description: Bounded GLTF/FBX/DAE/OBJ sidecar resource resolution, native/browser authorization, missing-resource diagnostics, and cleanup.
notes: Browser and native open paths normalize one primary plus selected relative sidecars into a bounded bundle; GLTFLoader, FBXLoader, and OBJLoader resolve only authorized local names.

Traversal, remote/data, duplicate/case-ambiguous, per-file/aggregate size, missing-resource, stale-load, and object-URL cleanup guards are implemented and tested. Texture loaders retain bundle URLs until image loads settle, remove failed maps before renderer/export work, and cap waits at two seconds.

FBX resolves only texture paths referenced by the file; unrelated selected maps are not guessed into material slots. OBJ supports one MTL bundle with relative textures; multiple material libraries and unsafe or unresolved resources fail closed while geometry-only OBJ remains supported.

issue__smf_resource_contract.description: SMF resource, allocation, offset, numeric, string, and fidelity boundaries across browser and native paths.
notes: Keep limits broad enough for committed fixtures but fail closed before allocation or numeric coercion.
Any limit change requires focused malformed-input coverage and current-state documentation.

tests__browser_authoring_formats.description: Archived compatibility route for the former combined browser authoring/format pack.
tests__browser_authoring_formats.archive_note: Use feature__rig_ik_pose, feature__skin_authoring, feature__animation_authoring, feature__fbx_support, and feature__theme_system.
notes: Generated indexed GLB coverage must pass SMF triangle-soup conversion and FBX re-import.
Strict snapshots remain opt-in and live beside their owning spec.

subsystem__load_editor_orchestration.description: Load/export intent ownership, editor snapshots, candidate construction, and stable cross-component event contracts.
notes: useLoadModel keeps its public return contract while pure snapshots and export candidates own focused policy; the codec-task lifecycle is routed through subsystem__export_pipeline.
Renderer and requestAnimationFrame ownership remain in ThreeViewport; mount listeners and TransformControls have explicit dispose owners.

Replacement decisions are centralized before byte materialization, async static append verifies current-root ownership before scene mutation, and editor history is capped at 100 entries/64 MiB with eviction status.

feature__humanoid_pose_review.description: Calibrated angular envelopes, Mixamo reference frames, read-only GLB scanning and report/reject diagnostics.
notes: Ranges are calibrated animation diagnostics, not medical constants or skin/contact/visual acceptance.
Profile application is routed separately through feature__retarget_profiles; private assets and generated reports stay excluded.
Caller-owned all-frame skin/contact and receiving-game acceptance is integration evidence, not a RustSMF completion contract.

subsystem__dev_process_lifecycle.description: Windows launcher ownership, npm resolution, preview-server startup, Tauri beforeDev cleanup, and orphan prevention.
notes: The launcher prefers the npm CLI bundled beside the active Node executable before falling back to PATH.
Playwright owns one build-and-preview server; independent test commands must not compete for port 5173.
Cleanup recognizes the exact normalized script argument of this checkout's Vite, Tauri CLI, or managed wrapper; ports, unrelated command arguments, and other checkouts do not confer ownership.
Dev exit cleanup runs only for dev tasks, including menu selections; Vite resolves through the installed package so workspace hoisting remains supported.

workflow__old_editor_reference.description: Archived GameMaker source and screenshots used only for deliberate parity research.
notes: Do not load the full archived source by default.
Use explicit file or screenshot globs only for a named parity question; the listed weight shaders are the selected-bone heat-map and paint-transport references.

workflow__fitted_rig.description: Explicit topology fitting, strict motion coverage, preserved skin bindings, and receipt-producing three-state comparison.
notes: Fitted verification requires exact requested clip identity and duration, samples every explicit regular grid time plus the terminal, and reports requested, completed, rejected, and worst-vertex evidence.
The viewer refuses clip intersections or shortened duration fallbacks, advances a remainder-preserving explicit-rate clock, and emits a current receipt for Quad/equal-height/exact-game comparison.
Mapped/unmapped skeleton colors, reversible mesh opacity, and one selected joint's axes and bend plane are read-only diagnostics validated against the manifest mapping and recorded in the receipt.
Generated fitted assets, private jobs, screenshots, and receiving-game artifacts remain outside context routes.

feature__runtime_pose_contact.description: Versioned Rust support-pose correction and conditioned-cycle transition baking, calibrated chains, vendoring contracts, and native/browser WASM proof.
notes: Canonical v1.rs is vendored verbatim where consumers cannot snapshot the RustSMF path crate; it uses existing libm 0.2.16.
Input is parent-first uniform-scale local TRS and one/two calibrated direct chains with independent limb subtrees; output is corrected full TRS, aligned joint orientations, and bounded diagnostics.
Calibrate the hip bend plane as pole × upper-axis and knee plane normal with the positive (hip-to-knee) × (knee-to-ankle) sign. No contact schedule or root travel is owned here.
